subject: POC kickoff: aligning prompt review, routing plan & load test window
messages:
From: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@acme-analytics.com>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@acme-analytics.com, ken.liu@acme-analytics.com
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC kickoff and hands-on prompt review

Hi Jordan —

Thanks for agreeing to run the POC. To make the kickoff productive, our internal team wants to cover three concrete things in the first working session: a quick inventory of prompts and expected structured outputs, the routing/fallback requirements (LLM variants for latency-sensitive paths), and a short traffic run (simulated load) to validate batching and KV cache behavior.

We have pulled an initial prompt list and attached it (acme_prompt_inventory.csv) — it’s only the first-pass inventory. Can Redwood propose a 2.5 hour block that includes a 60–75 minute hands-on prompt review, 30 minutes routing/design sync, and a 30–45 minute load window? Ideal dates for us next week are Tue (9/7) or Thu (9/9) in the US morning (10–12 PT).

Also: our security/compliance team requires a brief note on whether the load test will touch any PII and what data retention behavior Redwood will observe during the run.

Thanks — looking forward to aligning.

Best,
Maria Gonzalez
Director, Data Products
Acme Analytics

Attachment: acme_prompt_inventory.csv (CSV, 18 rows)

From: jordan_blake@redwood.ai <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC kickoff and hands-on prompt review

Maria —

Thanks for the prompt inventory — looks good as a starting point. Proposed plan:
- 2.5h working session broken into: 75m prompt review + mapping to structured outputs, 30m routing & fallback policy, 30–45m runbook-driven load window.
- Suggested test profile: staged ramp to 200 QPS peak for 10 minutes, then steady 50 QPS for 15 minutes to validate batching and cache hit behavior. We’ll run this against a short-lived sandbox model variant; no customer PII will be ingested into Redwood’s logs during the run unless you enable it.

Availability: Jordan (me) and Ben can do Thu 9/9 10:00–12:30 PT. Vivek can join from 10:30–12:30 PT. Lauren will lead the runbook and can be present the whole block.

I’ll attach a working mutual action plan and a traffic-runbook template for your review.

Can you confirm whether Thu 9/9 10:00–12:30 PT works for Acme and whether we should plan to run the load on the same day or a day after? Also, please let us know if any of the prompts in your CSV reference live customer IDs — if so we’ll provide instructions for syntheticization prior to the run.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Solutions Lead — Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_mutual_action_plan.docx, traffic-runbook-template.pdf

From: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@acme-analytics.com>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@acme-analytics.com, ken.liu@acme-analytics.com
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2027 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC kickoff and hands-on prompt review

Jordan —

Thu 9/9 10:00–12:30 PT works for our team. We prefer to run the traffic on a separate day to keep the review focused, so let’s schedule the load test for Fri 9/10 11:00–11:30 PT (short ramp + steady-state you proposed).

About PII: the CSV is synthetic — no live customer IDs. Ops will produce a separate synthetic payload for the load test; I’ll attach that to the runbook when ready.

One ask from procurement/security: can you add a short line in the MAP that states logs from the sandbox run will be retained for 7 days and then purged? If Redwood needs longer for debugging we can negotiate a scoped retention exception.

Thanks — Maria

Attachment: (none yet)

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@acme-analytics.com>, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 6 Sep 2027 07:55:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC kickoff and hands-on prompt review

Quick logistics note —

Jordan and team: I’ll run the prompt mapping breakout and prep the short evaluation harness (local traffic generator + synthetic payload). I’ll need a single repo or Drive folder where Acme will drop the final synthetic payload and any updated prompt rows. Maria, if you post the synthetic load CSV to the Drive link below by Thu EOD (9/9), we’ll run a dry-validation the evening of 9/9 and then execute the run 9/10 11:00–11:30 PT as agreed.

Two small confirmations for Acme ops:
- Do you want Redwood to capture request/response bodies in the sandbox logs? (Yes/No)
- If Yes, do you need us to hash or redact the prompt text at capture time?

Drive link: https://drive.redwood.com/s/ACME-POC-MAP

Thanks — will sync on the runbook 30m before the test.

Ben Carter
Senior Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference

Attachment: (none)

From: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@acme-analytics.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@acme-analytics.com, ken.liu@acme-analytics.com
Date: Mon, 6 Sep 2027 15:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC kickoff and hands-on prompt review

Ben —

Thanks, all confirmed. We will:
- Drop the synthetic payload into the Drive folder by Thu 9/9 5pm PT.
- For logs: please capture request/response bodies but redact any token-looking strings; hashing is fine for the user_id-like fields. Retention of 7 days is acceptable for now.

Looking forward to Thu’s session. I’ll send calendar invites to all participants once I confirm internal approvals.

Best,
Maria

Sent from my mobile
